column1: # limit-reset-phrases.tsv — real Claude usage-limit reset phrases.
# Harvested from real transcripts on 2026-08-12: every genuine limit event
# (synthetic + isApiErrorMessage) across five accounts — 262 of them, all
# 262 carrying a reset phrase, deduped to 175 distinct (now, phrase) pairs.
# Columns: now_epoch <TAB> phrase (verbatim) <TAB> expected_epoch
# The phrases and timestamps are MEASUREMENTS and are reproduced exactly;
# nothing identifying (session ids, paths, message bodies) was carried over.
# expected_epoch was computed with python's zoneinfo, NOT with the bash
# function these rows exist to test — an answer key the implementation did
# not write for itself.
# Two grammars appear, and which one you get is NOT predictable from the
# limit type: a weekly limit uses both.
#   resets 3:50am (Asia/Tokyo)             -> next occurrence, may cross midnight
#   resets Jul 27 at 5am (Asia/Tokyo)      -> dated, no year
# What this corpus does and does NOT cover. It is one person's transcripts, so
# it is a real sample, not a designed one:
#   covered     157 undated / 18 dated; 84 rows genuinely cross midnight, so the
#               "next occurrence" rollover is exercised by real data.
#   NOT covered every row is (Asia/Tokyo). These rows therefore cannot tell a
#               correct implementation from one that ignores the phrase's zone
#               and reads $TZ — on this machine the two agree. Nor is any DST
#               boundary here; Asia/Tokyo has no DST. Those cases are hand-built
#               in limit-reset.bats and must stay there.
